title: Automaquette: runlet bridge for adaptive admin shortcuts and taskified runbooks
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a lightweight 'runlet bridge' (Automaquette) that converts canonical runbooks into parameterized, permissioned admin shortcuts (runlets) for support engineers and first-line responders. The bridge should emit structured telemetry, support dry-run/simulate modes, enforce RBAC and approval gates, and allow safe execution inside the existing ops sandbox. Primary use cases: quick remediation shortcuts, context-aware fixes from alerts, and templated pre-approved patches for recurring incidents.
acceptance_criteria: Automaquette converts at least 3 canonical runbooks into typed runlets with parameter validation
Runlets execute within the ops sandbox and can be toggled into dry-run and live modes
RBAC and approval gates are enforced; attempts without permission are logged and blocked
Telemetry emitted per runlet execution: inputs, decision path, outcome, latency, and operator id
Safety fallback: on failure, runlet triggers a safe rollback or a no-op with annotated reason
Docs and quickstart guide published (Confluence + Console help) and a sample GitHub PR merged
tasks: Design runlet parameter schema and validation library (typed params, defaulting, sanitizers)
Implement runlet execution shim that calls existing admin API with RBAC checks
Integrate dry-run simulator and result diffing for safe previews
Wire telemetry events to ops-telemetry pipeline and dashboard (token costs and latency tags)
Add audit log entries to the central audit store and include KMS-encrypted artifacts where required
Create 3 sample runlets from high-value runbooks and ship sample PRs for review
End-to-end test suite covering success/failure/rollback and permission scenarios
Write Confluence runbook for SREs and a Console quickstart for support users
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Kickoff — aligned with PM on goal to reduce mean time to remediation for high-frequency incidents. Chosen runbooks for first pass: 'rotate-keystore-key', 'rebuild-serving-task', 'clear-prefetch-cache'. Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Automaquette+Overview

2026-02-18: Design review — Design asked for an inline compact UI for the Console; suggested collapsing advanced params behind an 'expert' toggle. Decision: implement compact mode v1, iterate after usage telemetry.

2026-02-22: Security review — Security flagged audit retention and KMS key-handling for attachments. Agreed to use customer KMS for Private tenants and company KMS for hosted runlets; audit records will include encrypted blobs and HMAC'd metadata.

2026-02-25: Engineering spike completed — prototyped typed param validation and dry-run simulator. Trade-off: typed schema adds upfront authoring cost but reduces runtime validation errors and UX confusion. Spike repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/automaquette-spikes/pull/6
2026-02-28: PM feedback — suggested adding 'preflight cost estimate' for tokenized runlets. Plan: a best-effort estimator using recent route/model profiles in the metrics store; low priority for MVP.

2026-03-01: Progress — core shim implemented, integrated RBAC checks, telemetry events emitted to ops-telemetry ingestion (event schema v2). Working on sample runlets and automated tests. Open PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-runlets/pull/42
